chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever comforts a person in bereavement, he will have a reward similar to that of the bereaved, without any reduction from the reward of the bereaved.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for comforting someone in grief according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith establishes the profound social and spiritual merit of *ta'ziyah* (condolences) in Shia tradition, emphasizing the concept of 'non-diminishing reward' (*min ghayr an yantaqisa min ajr al-musab shay'*). It illustrates the communal nature of spiritual merit, where the comforter shares in the bereaved's patience (*sabr*) without reducing their individual share, thereby reinforcing the interconnectedness of the Ummah in times of grief.
